headline: Start-up Veir has raised 110 million dollars to start making superconducting cables that carry power inside AI data centers.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a funding round for an unproven technology, with all claims from the company.
importance_line: Data center builders short of space and power may eventually get a more compact way to distribute electricity, but the technology has been shown at 3 megawatts and commercial deployments have yet to begin; the claims come from the company.
summary: The AI Insider reports, citing Veir, that its Series C round, co-led by Matter Venture Partners and Tyche Partners, brings total funding to 225 million dollars and will pay for manufacturing and first commercial projects. Veir's system uses superconducting cable (material that carries electricity with very little loss when cooled) to move more power through less space than copper, and the company has so far demonstrated a 3-megawatt system.
